the_signal.headline: Prompt testing frameworks move from nice-to-have to production baseline
the_signal.body: n8n's new systematic prompt testing framework addresses the real pain point: you can't ship AI workflows without regression detection. For GTM engineers deploying LLM-powered lead scoring, email generation, or qualification—prompt drift silently tanks conversion rates. This is the missing piece between reflection loops and production reliability.

thread_of_day.title: MCP vs. API: When to use Model Context Protocol in production workflows
thread_of_day.takeaway: MCP is becoming the protocol for stateful agent interactions; APIs remain better for request-response patterns—pick based on whether your revenue workflow needs persistent context or fire-and-forget calls.

quote.text: Process orchestration models (deterministic, dynamic, agentic) require different observability strategies—visibility across enterprise systems is non-negotiable for reliable revenue workflows.

whats_moving.context: Systematic testing frameworks now table stakes as teams realize silent prompt drift kills production LLM workflows without warning.
Agentic execution models require new observability primitives; deterministic + dynamic approaches no longer sufficient for multi-step revenue flows.
Model Context Protocol gaining traction as alternative to traditional APIs for stateful agent interactions in production systems.

act_on_this: Build a regression test suite for your highest-friction LLM prompt (lead scoring, qualification, email generation) this week—run it against last month's test cases to measure quality drift.
